metadata.note: The South and North Alabama Rail Road's only drawable own-name operation (Montgomery - Calera, a single-year 1871 anchor) and the L&N's Elmore - Wetumpka branch on the S&NA. The S&NA main line Decatur - Birmingham - Calera - Montgomery under the L&N (1872-1971), Amtrak's Floridian (1971-1979) and Gulf Breeze (1989-1995) are already drawn in ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson and gulf_breeze_amtrak.geojson and are not duplicated here.
metadata.ownership_split: S&NA (own operation, possibly via contractor Sam Tate) -> L&N on Montgomery - Calera at a date not established, latest 28 Sept 1872; the S&NA feature is an 1871 anchor and the L&N era is the existing L&N feature from 1872. The 30 Jun 1913 accounting change and the 21 Jan 1914 sale of S&NA property to the L&N are corporate only, not operator changes. The Wetumpka branch was L&N-operated throughout.
metadata.omitted: Calera - Birmingham under the S&NA (Nov 1871 - Sept 1872): drawable NONE, no S&NA-era passenger year confirmed. Decatur - 20 mi south and the 1872 gap: L&N from opening, covered by the existing L&N feature. Warrior Branch, Reeds branch, Helena - Acton and Hogeland Jct - El Vista spurs: no passenger evidence (Rule 1). Calera - Brock's Gap Confederate coal line 1863-65: freight/industrial only (Rule 1). Old main line Bangor - Blount Springs - Warrior - New Castle (block [7], L&N 1872-1914): an alignment correction to the existing L&N feature, deliberately not drawn here - see not_yet_sourced.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Elmore - Wetumpka trimmed to its confirmed passenger span 1906-1930; the branch's freight years to c.1973 are not drawn. The 1863-65 coal line, the Acton/El Vista spurs and the Reeds branch are excluded as freight/industrial.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN/ANCHOR spans: Montgomery - Calera (S&NA) is a single-year 1871 [ANCHOR] from one reminiscence (Armes 1910 p.225); the date the S&NA's own operation began and the date the L&N took over Montgomery - Calera are not established (best next sources: Montgomery Daily Advertiser / State Journal 1870-72, Poor's Manual 1871-73, Klein's L&N history 1972, Knoxville Daily Chronicle 5 Sep 1871 p.2 connections advertisement). Elmore - Wetumpka Branch start 1906 is [OPEN] (built 1879, station 1881, earlier passenger service unproven) and end 1930 is [OPEN] (NRHP 'until the 1930's'); whether a mixed train outlasted 'regular passenger service' is unknown. EXISTING-LAYER ISSUES NOT FIXED HERE (raised for the PR, not edited in this layer): (1) ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson draws Decatur - Birmingham on the post-1914 relocated main line or a straight line for 1872-1914, when trains ran on the old alignment via Bangor - Blount Springs - Reid's - Warrior - Kimberly - Morris - Cunningham - New Castle (block [7]: Fowler table 60 'Former route until 1915'; ICC revision 1910-1914; old alignment drawable 1872-1914); (2) the same layer's Nashville - Decatur and Decatur - Birmingham legs are ruled straight lines not named in geometry_quality; (3) its company string 'Louisville and Nashville Railroad (South & North Alabama Railroad)' differs from the plain L&N string (colour identical). First train into Birmingham: 11 Nov 1871 (HAER AL-214) vs 6 Nov 1871 (bhamwiki) - conflict recorded, not drawn.

properties.line: South and North Alabama: Montgomery – Calera
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: ~25 km/h for a newly built single-track Reconstruction-era road with stops; no timetable of the S&NA's own operation was found, so no time was converted.
geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror (railtrace degree tiles plus ways tagged old_railway_operator=L&N), routed with opstrace.py, 2026-11-10
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OSM over today's CSX S&NA South Subdivision (tagged old_railway_operator=L&N) from Montgomery Union Station to Calera; 63.3 mi traced, all on L&N-tagged track, against 62.70 mi documented (ICC valuation, 'Montgomery to Calera, Ala., 1870'; bhamwiki 63 mi). No straight-line leg; no approximated leg. Waypoints Montgomery, Elmore, Deatsville, Verbena, Clanton, Jemison, Calera all within 0.3 km of the line. Agrees with the existing L&N Birmingham - Montgomery trace in ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson (64.0 mi between the same points; within ~0.2 km except at the Montgomery terminal approach). LATER ALIGNMENT: drawn on the line as it survives in OSM (modern CSX track); any realignments since 1871 are not backed out, and the Montgomery end runs into Union Station (opened 1898) - the S&NA's 1871 Montgomery terminal is not located.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single-year anchor from ONE reminiscence: Armes, The Story of Coal and Iron in Alabama (1910) p.225, recounts chief engineer John T. Milner riding 'on the South and North from Montgomery to Calera' with his son, then on the Selma, Rome and Dalton to Chattanooga - undated in the text, placed in early 1871 by its context (after the Elyton Land Co. dealings of Dec 1870, before the L&N contract of 19 May 1871). LOW CONFIDENCE: it is second-hand, and Milner may have ridden a company or construction train rather than a public service. Service under the S&NA (or its contractor Sam Tate) very probably ran wider - track was complete by the end of 1870 and the L&N's May 1871 contract assignment excluded Montgomery - Elyton - but no other year is confirmed: 1870 is construction only and 1872 is unproven for S&NA operation. Do not widen this anchor without evidence; do not delete it to tidy the map. The L&N ran the route from 1872 (first through Montgomery - Louisville train 28 Sept 1872); that service is already drawn in ln_nashville_birmingham_montgomery.geojson. No timetable or frequency found - headway unknown, deliberately not estimated.
sources: Segment-level: Armes, The Story of Coal and Iron in Alabama (1910) p.225 (Milner's ride, the only positive passenger evidence) and p.249 (19 May 1871 assignment excluding Montgomery - Elyton); ICC valuation (Montgomery to Calera constructed 1870, 62.70 mi); Shelby Guide letter Jan 1870 via algenweb (construction south from Calera)

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OSM: 6.6 mi drawn from Elmore station on the main line, of which ~0.27 mi is the main line/wye at Elmore and 6.38 mi is the lifted branch itself (abandoned L&N-tagged way 7651285, TIGER-derived, ending at the Wetumpka depot). Branch traced against 6.23 mi documented (ICC valuation, 'Elmore to Wetumpka, Ala., 1879'; Fowler table 67 gives 6.1 mi). No straight-line leg; no approximated leg. The OSM way is TIGER-imported and unreviewed, so its position is only as good as TIGER's (typically within tens of metres for a surviving grade). Alignment is the branch as it stood when abandoned (after c.1973); no realignment is known.

segments.note: [OPEN] start and [OPEN] end. Drawn 1906 - 1930, the CONFIRMED span only. Start: the branch was built in 1879 (ICC) and the L&N built a small Wetumpka station in 1881 (NRHP), but the first year with positive passenger evidence is 1906, when the new depot was built with a passenger terminal, waiting rooms and a passenger agent's office (NRHP). Service very probably began earlier (possibly 1879/1881) - unproven, do not move earlier without evidence. End: the NRHP nomination says the depot served passengers 'until the 1930's when regular passenger service was terminated'; the bracket is 1930 - 1939 and the earliest year is taken. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggers Wetumpka (L&N) as freight only, consistent with no passengers by 1951. Freight continued after passenger service ended until the depot closed c.1973 (NRHP, 1975: 'closed two years ago') - context only, not drawn (Rule 1). L&N throughout: the S&NA company is recorded as builder (ICC) but never ran trains on it. Type of train (local or mixed) not found; headway unknown, deliberately not estimated.
sources: Segment-level: NRHP nomination, L&N Railroad Depot, Wetumpka (1975) for the 1906 passenger depot and the 1930s end of regular passenger service; ICC valuation for construction (1879, 6.23 mi); Fowler table 67; Feb 1952 Official Guide index (Wetumpka daggered freight-only)
